paper_000.title: Exploring the String Axiverse with Precision Black Hole Physics
key_contributions: Introduced the concept of BH superradiance as a probe of the String Axiverse
Defined the Regge trajectory in the mass-spin plane
Estimated observational signatures including gravitational waves from bosenova
Provided the QCD axion relation: mu_a = 6e-10 * (1e16/f_a) eV

paper_001.title: The Spectrum of the Axion Dark Sector, Cosmological Observable and BH Superradiance Constraints
key_contributions: Statistical framework for constraining multiple axion-like fields
Exclusion probability function for degenerate mass populations
Probed N_ax >= 30 exclusion for wide range of distribution parameters

paper_002.title: Black Hole Mergers and the QCD Axion at Advanced LIGO
key_contributions: Statistical analysis of BH spin-mass distributions for axion detection
Gravitational wave signals from axion annihilations and transitions
Updated exclusion from X-ray binary spin measurements: 6e-13 to 2e-11 eV

paper_003.title: Superradiant instabilities in astrophysical systems
key_contributions: Numerical evolution of massive scalar and vector fields around Kerr BHs
Confirmed superradiant instability for scalar fields
Showed vector (Proca) fields have much stronger instabilities
Maximum scalar instability at M*mu = 0.42 with tau ~ 10^7 M

impact_on_analysis.alpha_definition: Using M*mu/M_Pl^2 definition consistent with all papers
impact_on_analysis.regge_trajectory: Analytic formula derived from superradiance boundary condition
impact_on_analysis.timescale_comparison: Using Salpeter time (4.5e7 yr) for stellar BHs, 1 Gyr for SMBHs
impact_on_analysis.exclusion_zones: Consistent with literature ranges: ~1e-13 to ~1e-11 eV for stellar BHs
